title: Prompt bisect — cold-start regression notes
summary: Working notes from an ad-hoc bisect to isolate a cold-start regression affecting short-system prompts (<=20 tokens). Goal: determine whether the break is model-side, tokenization, or runtime cache warming behavior.
experiment_description: Observed a drop in pass-rate for short-system prompts starting 2025-01-28 after runtime optimization MR. This notebook walks through a manual bisect of prompt variants + runtime flags (kv-cache warm, batch size, quantization fallback) against a fixed test harness of 120 sampled requests.
hypotheses: H1: KV cache warm path changed semantics and returns stale/empty prefix leading to repetition
H2: Tokenization edge-case: some control characters in system prompt now get split differently, altering attention masks
H3: New kernel selection path triggers different positional embedding handling for short sequences
H4: Change in default temperature/biasing layering at serving runtime (unlikely but possible)
test_steps: 1) Run baseline (2025-01-25 golden container image) against sample set A (120 requests).
2) Run current production image (post-MR) against same sample set.
3) For failing cases, create minimal prompt variants by dropping tokens from the left and right (bisect).
4) Toggle runtime flags: kv_cache_warm=true/false, prefer_fast_kernels=true/false, quant_fallback=none/16-bit.
5) Re-run only failing prompts with each flag permutation to local dedicated node (isolated).
6) Capture raw logits + tokenization boundary traces for any divergence points.
7) Compare alignment to golden responses with a simple edit-distance + semantic check (embedding cosine).
sample_inputs: SYS: You are an assistant that summarizes in one sentence. User: Explain TLS to a non-technical manager.
SYS: Short system. User: Give a quick recipe for scrambled eggs.
SYS: <ctrl>Important: keep to one line. User: What's a haiku about clouds?
SYS: System: State the policy in two bullets. User: Company time-off policy summary?
sample_outputs_baseline: One-sentence summary: TLS creates an encrypted tunnel to protect data in transit.
Beat eggs, salt, pan, cook. (concise, single line)
Soft white clouds drift by, / silver lining hides the sun, / rain waits patiently.

- Employees accrue PTO monthly
- Manager approval required for >5 days
sample_outputs_current:
One sentence: TLS provides encryption and a handshake
One sentence: (duplication/repetition observed)
Beat eggs, salt, pan, pan, pan. (repetition)
Soft white clouds drift by, / silver lining hides the sun, / soft white clouds drift by. (repeat)

- Employees accrue PTO monthly
- 
- Manager approval required for >5 days
observations: Repetition/regeneration mostly on very short system prompts (<=12 tokens) or prompts containing an inline control token '<ctrl>'.
Baseline has clean single-line outputs; current shows duplicated spans or mid-output truncation with blank lines inserted.
Disabling kv_cache_warm reduces the repetition rate from ~24% to ~4% on the failing sample set.
Tokenization traces for the '<ctrl>' item differ: baseline tokenizes as single special token, current split into two tokens (leading to offset mismatch in attention).
Kernel selection toggles (prefer_fast_kernels=false) had minor effect except in one prompt where positional offset error persisted.
Raw logits show near-identical top-1 next-token probabilities until the divergence point where baseline has a stable token and current shows a near-uniform distribution (low confidence).
regression_findings: Primary contributor: change in tokenization behavior for a small set of control-like sequences; leads to misaligned KV cache keys when prefixed by short system prompts.
Secondary contributor: cache warm path returns an uninitialized KV map for certain tiny prefixes — makes logits collapse to low-confidence after a repetition and then the model repeats tokens.
Kernel selection change amplifies the effect for sequences where positional embedding indexing is sensitive (rare, but present).
quick_fixes_tried: Reverting KV warm patch in runtime - immediate drop in failures (but reintroduces throughput regression).
Applying tokenization normalization preprocessor to replace '<ctrl>' with a stable escape token - mitigates most cases.
Force prefer_fast_kernels=false for short-sequence routing - reduces failures but increases p99 latency by ~12ms.
Add a lightweight post-generation dedupe pass to collapse repeated n-grams (temporary hack).
recommendations: Prioritize a tokenization normalization step in serving layer that maps control-like tokens to canonical single tokens.
Short-term: disable kv_cache_warm on routes where system prompt length <= 16 until patch lands.
Medium-term: add unit tests that exercise short-system prompts + control characters against new kernel/selection logic.
Investigate kernel positional indexing assumptions with model-on-a-stick reproducer and add guard checks.
Customer-facing: prepare an incident note for teams using short system prompts; provide mitigation steps (prepend a sentinel token)
open_questions: Why did tokenization change between images? (tokenizer model/version drift or packaging bug)
Is there any dataset/model update that introduced new special tokens?
Can we design a cheaper kv_cache warm-check that validates key alignment before returning warmed cache?

2) Add failing-case unit tests to CI (owner: Naya).
3) Re-run the full 2k-sample smoke harness after tokenization fix in staging.
4) Draft an internal postmortem summarizing root cause and mitigations (owner: Jordan).
